DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: dilg.gov.ph 04 AUG 2016 DILG Legal Opinion No. 21 S. 2016 ACITY. LUCH R. GEMPIS, JR. City Government Department Head III Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlungsod Dear Atty. Gempis: This has reference to your letter dated 20 July 2016 requesting enlightenment from this Department on the following issues: 1. 2. 3. Whether the proceedings of the Sangguniang Panlungsod on 14 July 2016 are valid and legal despite the declaration of a recess sine c/léby the regular presiding officer until Tuesday, 19 July 2016 at 2:00 P.M. Or whether the same can be considered as usurpation of authority? Whether the nominations and voting of the different committee chairmanships and officers are valid and binding despite being conducted in the absence of the regular presiding officer and after the declaration of the presiding officer of the session in sine die? What are the legal effects if any on the salaries and emoluments of the staff under the Committee Chairmanships and officers as to their effectivity and commencement? Based on your letter, during the regular session of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Manila on 14 July 2016, the regular Presiding Officer (Vice-Mayor) declared the session in recess until 19 July 2016 (Tuesday) at 2 P.M. Then, the regular Presiding Officer and other Sangguniang Panlungsod Members left the session hall. The stenographers and staff of the Secretariat had likewise already left the session hall. Thereafter, a group of Sangguniang Panlungsod members resumed and conducted the continuation of the session immediately after. The remaining Sangguniang Panlungsod Members (still representing the majority of the august body) nominated the different committee chairmanships and officers despite the absence of' the regular Presiding Officer and several Sangguniang Panlungsod Members. Hence, your above-stated queries.

Attached to your subject letter is a certified true copy of the Transcript of the Stenographic Notes (TSN) dated 14 July 2016, until the Presiding Officer had declared a recess, for our perusal. As there is no clear and express rule on the power of the regular Presiding Officer to adjourn or suspend sanggunian sessions under Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 , and its Implementing Rules and Regulations, the Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) of the concerned sanggunian, that is, the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Manila shall be relevant in the present controversy. Section 40 of the IRP of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Manila states: SECTION 40. ADJOURNMENT AND SUSPENSION OF SESSIONS—Sessions shall be adjourned by the Presiding Officer upon motion of the Majority Floor Leader when all the business in the agenda has been taken up or when the question of quorum is raised and no quorum was re-established thereafter. In case of lack of quorum at the start of the session, extreme emergencies, serious and uncontrollable disorder, public disturbances and other unavoidable circumstances, such declaration of adjournment maybe made "motu propio" by the Presiding Officer. The Presiding Offcer may also. during the session. declare at any time a suspension or recess of short intervals of not more than fifteen (15) minutes except on recess sine die. (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the foregoing, as a general rule, sessions are adjourned by the Presiding Officer, upon motion of the Majority Floor Leader. Also, the Presiding Officer is given the power to unilaterally declare at any time a suspension or recess of short intervals of not more than fifteen (15) minutes. In case such suspension or recess shall last for more than fifteen (15) minutes or "recess sine diel", then the declaration of the Presiding Officer shall be upon the approval Of the sanggunian members, thus in accordance with the above-stated general rule. Thus, the act of the Vice Mayor, as the regular presiding officer, of unilaterally declaring a "recess sine die" and, apparently under the objection of the majority of the members of the Sanggunian, suffers from legal infirmity. From the foregoing, it follows that the session, which continued after the "recess sine did' was valid and binding and the acts performed by its members, despite being Black's Law dictionary defines the latin word "sine die" - "without day or "a meeting that has been indefinitely adjourned where no date has been made for a resumption."

conducted in the absence of the presiding officer and several other sanggunian members, was also valid, binding and legal. As to the salaries and emoluments of the staff under the respective committees of the sanggunian will depend on their respective appointments and assumption to office. We hope to have guided you accordingly. AU e truly yours, Undersecretary DI - OUSI.G 2016-08•01-0• 841 opy furnished: DIR. MA.
